reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 discusses wear behavior of different alloys without mentioning oxide film disruption. E2 describes protective oxide scales that reduce corrosion over time, contradicting the proposed breakdown cycle. E3 notes passive film breakdown under pitting attack but does not link it to mechanical wear or a feedback cycle. No evidence supports the claimed stress/temperature-induced oxide disruption or the wear-corrosion feedback mechanism.
premises: High-temperature wear events cause local, transient peaks in mechanical stress and temperature.
These peaks disrupt a protective oxide film on the alloy surface.
Oxide film breakdown exposes the reactive metal substrate to the corrosive environment.
Enhanced corrosion accelerates wear, creating a positive feedback cycle.
This cycle causes a nonlinear, threshold increase in total degradation.
